title: Here's when the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are rumored to go on pre-order
description: Apple is unveiling the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, along with the iPhone Ultra, on September 9. That's a Wednesday. If you know Apple, you know that the company loves to commence pre-orders for new iPhones on the Friday of the week they are announced. However, this year there's a wrinkle. The Friday after the event is September 11, and for obvious historical reasons, given that it's a US-based company, Apple is now rumored to alter its plans and actually start taking pre-orders for the new iPhones on September 12, which is a Saturday. title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE in for review
description: The Galaxy FE models have always enjoyed the attention of loyal and savvy Galaxy fans, but Samsung may be cutting it a bit too close with the Galaxy S26 FE. We called it the "Galaxy S26 AI and the Galaxy S25 FE Part 2 in our announcement news, and we still stand by that. To start with, the Galaxy S26 FE is nearly identical, spec-for-spec, with its predecessor. The major aspects of the phone are the same: the same 6.7-inch screen, triple camera system, battery and charging, and overall feel in the hand. description: Apple hiked the prices of all of its hardware products back in June. As we're all anxiously waiting for the company to make its iPhones more expensive too, in the meantime, it has made two of its services more expensive. We're talking about Apple TV (previously known as Apple TV+) and the Apple One all-encompassing subscription, which already got more expensive last month for its family and premier plans. title: Google Pixel 11 in for review
description: Last year was a big step for the Pixel 10, which gained a zoom camera (but downgraded the main camera), but this year, Google is keeping things simpler (and less innovative). The Google Pixel 11 is a straightforward yearly specs update. It keeps the body mostly unchanged; the screen is the same 6.3-incher, the battery is more or less the same, and so is the charging. What is new is the chipset - the 3nm Tensor G6, and the main camera, which packs a larger 1/1.56-inch main sensor (vs 1/2.0-inch on the Pixel 10), bringing it closer to the Pixel 9's 1/1.31-inch main unit.
